scene_report.narration_text: In March 2024, Kendrick Lamar ignited a massive controversy by rejecting the idea that he, Drake, and J. Cole were rap's Big Three.
scene_report.main_action: Sitting on a stand in a recording booth

scene_report.narration_text: His message was simple: there is only one king.
Drake fired back with the track Push Ups, mocking Kendrick's career and reputation.
Kendrick responded by unleashing Euphoria, a brutal six-minute diss track attacking his rival.
The conflict turned personal when Drake released Family Matters, making explosive allegations about Kendrick's private life.
Less than an hour later, Kendrick shocked everyone with Meet the Grahams, firing back with disturbing allegations about Drake and his family.
On May 4, Kendrick dropped the devastating track Not Like Us, accusing Drake of serious misconduct.
While Drake denied the claims, the song exploded across the internet, becoming a global anthem.
Ultimately, a song created to destroy a rival won five Grammy Awards, cementing this as one of hip-hop's most unforgettable rivalries.
